Design review notes

This is deliberately a larger and more cinematic experiment than the previous hero. The opening gives the seasonal Brother Vitus artwork almost the entire viewport, while the typography, navigation and calls to action make it clear that Vitus is creative software.

The main idea: the living chronicle becomes a working world. Scroll from the seasonal scene into a connected, illustrative map-and-lore software window. The idea can be executed with actual product captures once they're ready.

Seedance clips: use the season buttons to choose a still, then click “Preview Seedance clip” to test your own MP4/WebM file in the hero. Your selected video is played locally in the browser and is not uploaded. Each season can have a different local clip. The videos will not be saved when you close the tab.

Honest trade-off: this is visually stronger but shows less literal application UI in the first viewport than the previous concept. Consider how much of the app demonstration should peek into view on desktop and mobile.

Production requirements: prefer short muted loops; use poster images; reserve one clear primary action; ensure overlays remain readable in all seasons; preload only the current loop; pause when offscreen; honour reduced-motion preferences; and never claim that a prototype UI is a real application screenshot.

All illustrations were supplied for this review. This is not a deployed website.
